title: Central groupoids, central digraphs, and zero-one matrices A satisfying A^2 = J
contribution: Surveys and re-proves the theory of 0-1 matrices with A^2 = J, disproves Fletcher's row/column multiplicity conjecture for k >= 4, introduces rank-changing 'switches' that give a short proof of Shader's rank theorem, and proves embedding and counting results for sub-central groupoids.
problem_entry: Enters Hoffman's open classification problem (p. 3, open for k >= 4 p. 5) sideways: short proofs of basics, a specific conjecture (Fletcher, pp. 5-6) and a new local move (switches, §3).
key_idea: A switch (complementing a 2x2 identity submatrix) preserves A^2 = J iff index/row/column conditions hold and changes rank by at most one (Thm 3.1, pp. 7-8); an explicit switch schedule climbs from the standard matrix to maximal rank one unit per step (Thm 3.3, pp. 8-12).
assumptions: Pure combinatorial model A_n (0-1, A^2 = J_n, nonempty iff n = k^2, p. 4), up to permutation similarity; switch-reachability of all of A_n is an open conjecture (Conj. 3.2, p. 8); smoothness/noise n/a.
proof_devices: A^3 computed two ways forces equal row/column sums; Perron root and trace give k diagonal ones (Thm 2.1, p. 4)
Diagonalizable A^2 bounds nilpotent Jordan blocks by 2; PSD AA^t with trace k^3 gives the rank lower bound and its equality case (Thm 2.2, p. 5)
Parametric block counterexample for all k >= 4 with explicit k = 4 instance (Thm 2.3, p. 6)
Brualdi-Ryser decomposition into permutation matrices after a loop/two-cycle count (Lemma 2.4, Thm 2.5, pp. 6-7)
Cyclic invariance of spectra XY ~ YX to reduce words (Thm 2.6, p. 7)
Rank-one update bounds rank change by one (Thm 3.1, p. 8)
Upper-bound-plus-attainment: final rank = start + number of switches forces +1 per switch (p. 11)
Disjoint touched-row and touched-column index sets certify legality of the whole schedule in any order (p. 10)
Leading-ones positions certify linear independence of row-space vectors (pp. 11-12)
Block multiplication for the (k+1)^2 embedding (Thm 4.1, p. 15); referee-supplied uniqueness-of-walks proof (Thm 4.3, pp. 15-16)
experiments: No timing experiments; computer enumeration from the REU report gives the 6 classes of A9 (p. 4), checks Conjecture 4.2 on the 101 matrices of A16 and for k = 2, 3 (p. 15); maximal-rank A16 and A25 printed in full (pp. 12-13); programs public (p. 3).
positioning: Partly a survey with short proofs (p. 2); builds on Hoffman, Knuth, Shader, Fletcher (pp. 3, 5, 8, 16); judges Shader's proof by its length of checks rather than attacking it (p. 8); flags each new result (pp. 5, 7); credits referees with Thm 4.3's proof (p. 16).
writing: Four-sentence abstract (p. 2); every construction followed by its smallest concrete instance (pp. 3-6, 12-13); intuition remark after a terse proof (p. 11); numbered Problems and Conjectures placed where they arise (pp. 7, 8, 14, 15).
limits_future: Classification for k >= 4 open (p. 5); Conjecture 3.2 unresolved (p. 8); Conjecture 4.2 verified only for small cases (p. 15); Problems 2.7, 3.5, 3.6 posed (pp. 7, 14).

method_links.note: Analogue only: a structured instance family built on purpose to break a conjecture, with the smallest member exhibited; counterexamples, not solver test sets.

title: Determinant optimization on binary matrices
contribution: Unifies the max-odd-2x2-submatrix problem and the D-optimal max det(A^tA) problem on +-1 matrices as two orders of tr C_k(AA^t), re-proves known cases via Hadamard deletions, settles n = 9 by pruned enumeration, and finds best-known solutions for n = 17, 21, 25, 41 with multistart descent and tabu search.
problem_entry: Takes the one case left unsolved by Marks et al. (2003), n x n with n = 4k+1, and brings computation and heuristics to it (p. 2).
key_idea: Compound matrices turn both problems into maximizing tr C_k(AA^t) = E_k(eig(AA^t)) at k = 2 and k = n, so majorization and Hadamard deletions give bounds (pp. 3-10); where proof stops, pruned enumeration (pp. 11-14) then sign-flip local search and two-list tabu search (pp. 15-17).
assumptions: Entries +-1; Hadamard conjecture assumed for optimal values (pp. 2-3, 6); equivalence under transpose, permutations, sign changes (p. 5); bound U assumes an Ehlich-type matrix exists (p. 16); smoothness/noise n/a.
proof_devices: Nonzero entries of the second compound counted as tr(C2 C2^t)/4 = E2(eig(AA^t))/4 (Thm 1, pp. 3-4)
Majorization bound with equality iff AA^t = nI (Thm 2, p. 4)
Normalize a Hadamard matrix so a row and column are all ones, delete them, read the spectrum of (n+1)I - J (Thm 5, p. 7); block analogues for two and three deletions (Thm 6, p. 8; Thm 10, p. 10)
Per-pair agreement/disagreement counting M(A) = sum k_ij * kbar_ij (Thm 3, eq. (3.1), pp. 5-6)
Diophantine parity argument fixing the first three rows in the 9x9 case (pp. 11-12)
Catalogue of inner-product multisets any improving matrix must have (Table 1, pp. 12-13) used to prune enumeration; empty enumeration proves A9 optimal (p. 13)
experiments: n = 17, 21, 25, 41; structured start 2I - J plus 100 random restarts; report S, average, best, bound U and % gap (Tables 2-4, pp. 16-18); tabu (L1, L2) chosen from a 16-point grid with seed 123456789 printed in Appendix B (pp. 24-25) but tuned on the reported instances with unstated selection rule; 1000-restart run (p. 18); no CPU times.
positioning: Connects Hadamard determinant, D-optimal design and Turan-number literatures (p. 2); Marks et al. (2003) as immediate predecessor credited for three cases and bounds (pp. 7-9); heuristics taken from Glover's tabu search (pp. 16-17); Hedayat-Zhu misspelled 'Heyadat' (pp. 9, 10, 13, 18).
writing: Synoptic abstract states scope and best-known claim (p. 1); each case opens with what is known and by whom (pp. 7-9); explicit hand-off from proof to heuristics (p. 14); hedged empirical readings (p. 18); a citation slip attributing Marshall-Olkin sections to Marks et al. (p. 4).
limits_future: No optimality proof for n >= 17 (p. 14); relation between Problem 1 and 2 optima unclear, disjoint at n = 17 (p. 18); future: eigenvalue structure of optima (pp. 19-20), integer programming and the continuous relaxation -1 <= a_ij <= 1 for bounds and starts (p. 20).

method_links.note: Both heuristics share move set, structured start and 100 restarts, and the paper prints where the simpler method can win and a feature that did not help; but tabu parameters were tuned on the evaluation instances with an unstated selection rule (full grid reported).

Results measured as gap to a bound U whose validity rests on an unproved existence assumption, stated beside every table; the 1000-restart plateau is read either as optimality or as the method's limit. States the yardstick's assumption rather than auditing it.

transferable: Rewrite a counting objective on +-1 matrices as a symmetric function of eig(AA^t) via compound matrices and use majorization for bounds with equality cases (pp. 3-4).
Normalize by symmetries so a row and column are all ones, delete them, and read off the closed-form spectrum of cI - J (p. 7).
Prune exhaustive search by fixing rows up to symmetry, a pre-derived catalogue of structures any improving solution must have, and a goal value after each added row (pp. 11-14, 19).
For combinatorial local search, run one structured start plus many random restarts, report start value, average, best, bound and % gap, and print the full parameter grid with seed (pp. 15-18, 24-25).
